exceptions.what: The device record (name, manufacturer, model, software version) of the ECCO Intelligence device
exceptions.note: The registry is read through a websocket call. The software version is also published as the status attribute integration_version.

Incidents of Intelligence's advice log: each time writing its advice failed or could not be read back (when, attempts, cycles missed, kind of error). Only the newest are kept; one open at a restart is lost, so an empty list is no proof of a complete log. Nothing is applied. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
Whether a cycle is running right now. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The scheduling state: refresh rules, retries, backoff, poll tracking and timers. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
How many cycles of each kind have run and how many were refused or failed. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The total duration of the last cycle. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
A summary of recent cycle durations and counts. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The Home Assistant entity ids the owner's site file maps to the cycle's inputs. The integration's own diagnostics download redacts it as a site value, so Geek Mode withholds it as well.
The start-up grace period before the first cycle. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
A summary of the last cycle, including the notes about each input source. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
How long each step of the last cycle took. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The last scheduled slot a cycle ran for. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The last write to the integration's own results store. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
How recently the input data was seen to change. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).

The engineering limits (proposed values, not owner decisions) the integration runs with. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).

The full start-up self-test with PASS, INFO, WARN and FAIL results. The status attribute self_test carries only each check's PASS or FAIL result; the download also holds the INFO and WARN results and their texts. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
Whether the integration has finished starting. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).
The time one cycle may take before it is abandoned. Not in any state or attribute: showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity (a contract change request).

exceptions.what: Entity-registry facts: unique id, disabled or hidden flags, recorder exclusions
exceptions.note: The registry is read through a websocket call. By contract the unique id equals the entity's object id.

exceptions.what: Contract field 'scorecard_report' (an internal result of one cycle)
exceptions.note: The scorecard report of one cycle is kept in the integration's own database, never published, and never contains a recommendation. Showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity.

exceptions.what: Home Assistant and integration log lines
exceptions.note: Logs are files, not states. Showing them would need a read-only log endpoint and a redaction pass: a separate security decision, not a card feature.

exceptions.what: The persistent notifications the three alert automations create
exceptions.note: A notification is not a state. Their texts are fixed (see the three automations); the alert strip shows the same conditions from the entity states.

exceptions.what: History and long-term statistics of these entities (the Home Assistant recorder)
exceptions.note: History is not a state: it is read with a history request, and Geek Mode makes no request of any kind. The integration also keeps the advice, input ages and self-test attributes and the timestamps out of the recorder, so history would lack them. Showing history would need an explicit decision to allow one read-only history query.
The integration's own diagnostics download redacts this site value; Geek Mode never shows it.
The integration's own diagnostics download redacts this site value; Geek Mode never shows it.

exceptions.what: The scorecard database of past cycles (scorecard.sqlite3 in the integration's state folder)
exceptions.note: A file, not a state. It holds accuracy bookkeeping only (never a recommendation). Showing it would need a new read-only diagnostic entity.

exceptions.what: The owner's site file (site.local.json) that maps the cycle's inputs to the owner's own entities
exceptions.note: It is site data (entity ids, tariffs, device names) and is never shown. The integration's own diagnostics redact the entity map for the same reason.

exceptions.what: The 28 site readings one cycle consumes (battery state, capacity, tariff tables, forecasts, ...)
exceptions.note: They are the owner's other entities, read through the site file's mapping. Intelligence publishes only their names and ages (the status attribute input_ages), never their values. Their values belong to those entities' own tabs.

exceptions.what: The context of each state change (which user, automation or integration caused it)
exceptions.note: A context can hold user ids. The Intelligence entities are written only by the integration, so it would add nothing.
